reason: E1 and E2 directly confirm that replacing Co with Cr in AlCoFeNi leads to B2+BCC decomposition, increased coercivity, and reduced magnetization, matching the hypothesis's core premises. The cited evidence also supports the processing conditions and microstructural mediator, though the specific mechanism of antiferromagnetic Cr promoting pinning is inferred rather than explicitly demonstrated.
premises: AlCoFeNi baseline is single-phase B2 at high temperature
Substituting Co with Cr promotes decomposition into B2 + BCC
This decomposition increases coercivity and reduces saturation magnetization
The effect holds under standard casting and ~1000 °C annealing
Cr-rich regions and phase boundaries act as domain wall pinning sites
